body: This brings up a question in my mind:  Should the stronger model get the work or guidance in its prompt based on the weaker model's efforts?  If the weaker model halucinates something, this could poison the context of the stronger model and spoil the result, when on his own he may have provided the right result without the weaker model's efforts.

Maybe an approach which avoids us needing an obstacle task course here.  In the obstacle approach though, each model has his own green field, I'd assume.  Not sure.  Maybe still worth a GH issue to get the agent team to chime in its worthiness.

body: So are you leaning against waves in one plan?  Are you suggesting that your approach is necessary because the phases are quite complicated?

Note that I have a work MacBook today that has the same specs, except it has 128GB unfied memory, whereas due to prices, the one I purchased is only 64GB unified memory.  Honestly, my memory limitation with my home setup will cause me to work harder to improve local inference support in Guardrails, so I see it as a challenge.
We can already be using the work MacBook.  Therefore, Phase 2 shouldn't be gated at all.

Right. It is listed precisely because it is unbuilt: naming the ladder's grain now is what keeps the two complementary if it ever ships, and section 8's single-owner rule is where that accounting is actually enforced. Without the row, a ladder designed later would re-derive its own record of what each model did, and then two mechanisms disagree about the same history. Added a paragraph under the table saying so.

It bites harder than it first looks: a cold load is tens of seconds and belongs to the machine, not the model, so an unrecorded cold start is charged to whichever model happened to be evicted last. That is the difference between a fair speed comparison and a coin flip.

Good question, and the answer is worse than I assumed. I checked: TaskExecutor.cs:1092 journals a scope violation as AttemptOutcome.GuardrailFailed with only Summary = 'write-scope violation: <paths>' to distinguish it, and the check runs BEFORE any guardrail. So today it is in the same bucket as a failed test, and an ETL trusting the enum would fold an instruction-following failure into a capability one. Added write-scope violation as its own taxonomy row plus a warn block: the corpus splits them at ingest using the summary prefix and the distinct GuardrailFailureFingerprint, and Phase 1 should weigh a first-class outcome value.

Filed as #537 with an explicit brief for the agent team rather than a design I made up. It asks them to answer, in order: is it worth building at all given the replay bench already exists (with the case AGAINST stated as strongly as the case for); where it lives (your two candidates, plan-breakdown training mode vs a harness run option, plus a third - a bench sibling that takes a suite - and the plan-breakdown option gets particular scrutiny, since breakdown authors tasks and does not run them); green field per model or shared start; what goes in the course and what stops it rotting; how course rows relate to production rows; and what stops a fixed course becoming a target that gets optimized against. Adversarial pass by a non-authoring agent required before they report, per the #467 rule. Also cross-referenced from section 7 of the plan.

Same issue - #537 - since this and your note on the stratification line are the two halves of one question. Your green-field assumption is question 3 in the brief, stated as your assumption and flagged to be confirmed or overturned explicitly with the isolation mechanism named (worktree per model, per attempt, or a full clone). I have added a note to section 7 framing the two honestly: replay is free and contaminated, a course is expensive and clean, and a small course anchoring the scale while replay supplies volume is a plausible third answer.

Agreed, and taken. Section 6 now says a local model is not free: the hardware is sunk and unattributable, but the electricity is not, so an estimated energy figure (configured dollars-per-kWh times machine draw times measured wall time) is carried. It is labelled an ESTIMATE and never summed into a reported costUsd - same projection-versus-measurement line #528 has to hold. Your underlying point is the sharper one: printing zero invites a conclusion the physics does not support.

This is a real fork and it was unstated - thank you. The stronger model can start from the weaker one's work plus retry feedback (today's shape, with #306 salvage), from a clean base, or from a hybrid carrying failed guardrail names but not the weak diff. Your trap is that attempt 2 inherits a FRAME: a hallucinated premise in the transcript is a strong prior the stronger model may defend rather than discard, and the outcome cannot show that it did. The design decision belongs to #228's ladder, so I have written it up there as a comment rather than deciding it in this plan. What this plan contributes is the datum that settles it empirically - section 3.1's retry context makes 'escalated with inherited context' and 'escalated clean' two comparable populations over identical fingerprints. Note added to section 8.

Not leaning against waves, and not about complexity - I should have said why. A waved plan is right when the whole scope is known and merely needs ordering, and if all four phases were known one waved plan would be the better shape. These are split because Phase 0's first real report changes what Phases 1 to 3 SHOULD be: which instrumentation gap matters most, whether a bench is even needed, what a graduation threshold should be. None of those can be authored honestly before the corpus exists. Phase 0 alone is fully known today, which is why it is the only one cut as an issue (#535). Note added at the top of section 11.

That memory gap has a direct design consequence, so I have folded it in rather than just noting it: 64GB and 128GB will run the same model NAME at different quantizations, which means they are not the same model and their rows must not pool. The machine profile in section 3.1 now records unified memory explicitly, alongside the digest and quantization in the model fingerprint. Your constraint is also the more interesting test case - a setup that has to work hard for local inference produces sharper evidence about where local actually holds up than one with headroom to spare.

Corrected. Phase 2 now says it is NOT gated on new hardware - the 128GB MacBook is available today and the only real dependency is plan 28's openai-compat runner (#223). I had smuggled a hardware assumption into a software dependency.
